newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-No budget problem in Australian fiscal error.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-No budget problem in Australian fiscal error.

text.p: An error in Australia's latest fiscal calculations had no implications for the government's own budget, Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp said on Thursday.
"The errors identified by the Department of Finance do not relate to the budget sector of government" Kemp told the Senate.
Treasury said on Wednesday the department had underestimated the so-called general government deficit by A$1.2 billion, adding that the errors had occured in its spreadsheets.
The general government deficit is the sum of deficits for the budget sector -- typically, departments -- and some off-budget operations, such as the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.
The number, issued wrongly in last month's mid-year review of government finances, is routinely published to meet an accounting standard.
Very few analysts take notice of it, however.
The error made no difference to the government's main fiscal number, the underlying budget balance.

Treasury's mid-year financial estimates forecast that the underlying budget deficit -- which excludes asset sales -- would be A$8.5 billion in the fiscal year to June 1997, not the A$5.6 billion projected in the August budget.
